A Django CSRF 403 on `hx-post` after moving a form into a partial usually means the request no longer carries the token: the partial has no `{% csrf_token %}`, or the token is sent via `hx-headers` (`X-CSRFToken`) on an element that isn't an ancestor of the form anymore, or the partial is rendered without the request so no token is available. Having it in the base template only helps if the form actually inherits it. Action: look at the partial and base template to see how the token is supplied and how the view renders the partial, then fix that one spot.

They're not the same. Keep-alive just reuses one TCP connection for sequential requests, so each connection still handles one request at a time and browsers open several connections per host to get parallelism. HTTP/2 multiplexing interleaves many concurrent request/response streams over a single connection (binary frames, header compression), so a slow response doesn't block the others at the HTTP layer, although TCP-level head-of-line blocking remains, which HTTP/3 addresses. Action: none needed; happy to point at where this would show up in our setup if useful.

The common thread: with `verbatimModuleSyntax` on, TypeScript requires imports that are only used as types to be written as `import type { X }` or `import { type X }`. Every error is a type (ClientRow, SortKey, FastifyPluginAsync, and so on) imported as a normal value import. It's mechanical, and an autofix exists in most linters (an import-type rule), so you don't need to hand-edit them. `using x = getResource()` declares a resource that is automatically disposed when the block exits, including on a throw, by calling `x[Symbol.dispose]()`. Multiple `using` declarations are disposed in reverse order. `await using` does the same with `Symbol.asyncDispose` for async cleanup. It needs the right `lib`/target settings, and the runtime needs `Symbol.dispose` (recent Node versions, or a polyfill), so check which Node we run.
